faq.q: How can I tell if someone feels left out?
faq.a: Look for someone sitting or standing alone, watching others play, looking down, or being quiet a lot. When unsure, you can just ask: Do you want to join?

faq.q: What can I say to include someone?
faq.a: Try: Want to sit with us? Do you want to play? We need one more player! Simple and friendly is best.
asks: What do I say to someone sitting alone?

faq.q: What if my friends do not want to include them?
faq.a: You can say kindly: Let's give them a chance, it is not nice being alone. You can also spend some time with the new person yourself.
asks: Tell me about the Keep including

faq.q: Why does being left out hurt?
faq.a: Humans need to belong. Research shows being left out activates brain areas linked to pain, so it really does hurt.
asks: Why do I feel so bad when I am left out?

faq.a: A bench in some playgrounds where children can sit if they want someone to play with. Others see it and come over to invite them.

facts: A 2003 brain-scan study by Naomi Eisenberger and colleagues found that being left out of a ball-tossing game activated brain areas also linked to physical pain.
The buddy bench idea spread widely after a US student, Christian Bucks, brought one to his school in 2013.

quiz.say: You see a new classmate sitting alone at lunch. What could you do?
quiz.why: A simple invitation helps someone feel they belong.

quiz.say: What is the first step to including someone?
quiz.why: You need to notice someone feels left out before you can help.
